pieces.title: Tides Remember
pieces.summary: A forgotten pine cabinet becoming a weather-worn relic of tide, salt, copper, and sea glass.
pieces.story: Found in warm pine with a heart cut into its frame, this small cabinet is being rebuilt as though it spent decades beside the Atlantic. Charcoal shadows, broken turquoise, pale seafoam, visible grain, and aged copper will preserve its history while giving it an entirely new life.
pieces.materials: Pine, water-based furniture paint, acrylic glazes, copper accents, satin protective finish

pieces.title: Aurora After Dark
pieces.summary: A slender console table waiting to carry turquoise, violet, ember, and antique gold across its surface.
pieces.story: The quiet frame will remain dark and elegant while the tabletop becomes the sky: layered teal, violet, burgundy, ember-orange, and gold. The finished piece will feel less like painted furniture and more like a functional landscape.
pieces.materials: Wood, charcoal furniture paint, acrylic glazes, metallic accents, satin protective finish

pieces.title: Scrapyard Freddy Mk I
pieces.summary: An active, distressed animatronic-style wearable puppet build with hand-operated mechanisms and a modular fitted chassis.
pieces.story: An oversized, scrap-built Freddy character that explores mechanical puppetry, expressive eyes and jaw movement. Previously recorded as Nightmare Freddy; the historical project and fitted harness records are preserved.
pieces.materials: Wearable backplate, structural supports, mechanical linkages, bungee cord, sculptural shell and weathered finishes (final inventory to verify)
pieces.buildNotes: Active build. Eye and jaw linkage and arm controls have been prototyped; verify current construction and safety testing before declaring complete.
buildSteps: Existing wearable backplate and structural support
Turnable eye control using inverted baby-scooter handle
Planned foam exterior and final wear testing

pieces.title: Project Sprite — Wearable Prototype
pieces.summary: Long-term wearable and spatial-computing system exploring smart glasses, anchored interfaces, environmental sensing, gestures and AI assistance.
pieces.story: A modular research programme rather than a finished object. Physical prototypes may include smart-glasses frames, sensors, gesture input, edge hubs and environmental interaction devices. The software vision lives within the wider Sprite / S.A.G.E. / AetherOS ecosystem.
pieces.materials: Research candidates: 3D-printed housings, small displays or optics, cameras, sensor modules, microcontrollers, battery systems and replaceable mounts; no bill of materials approved.
buildSteps: Document use cases and privacy boundaries
Choose one isolated wearable hardware prototype
Test fit, power, temperature and ergonomics
Reassess integration with S.A.G.E. and spatial workspaces
pieces.buildNotes: Umbrella research project. Record distinct physical prototypes as child instances when they exist. No complete wearable device claimed.

versions.notes: Concept archived from earlier Sprite/NOVA/NOMAD planning; no hardware completion claimed.

pieces.title: NOVA — Flying AI Companion
pieces.summary: Flubber/Weebo-inspired personal AI flying companion with a friendly face, responsive lights and eventual spatial awareness.
pieces.story: NOVA is the named Flubber-inspired autonomous companion drone concept, earlier explored as Weebette and in later creative notes as Lumen. A fantasy-like flying familiar: playful in appearance, practical in sensing, designed to work with Project Sprite and S.A.G.E. Distinguish early explorations and naming from confirmed fabrication.
pieces.materials: Research candidates: enclosed or ducted-fan micro-drone platform, 3D-printed shell, lightweight face display or LEDs, camera, proximity sensors, docking hardware; flight electronics to be selected.
buildSteps: Define safe indoor proof-of-concept and airframe limits
Bench-test lighting and animated face without flight
Evaluate flight stability and safe autonomous behavior
Document docking, battery handling and interaction concepts
pieces.buildNotes: Concept only; do not depict as a working autonomous flying robot. Prototype in simulation and controlled environments, respecting local drone rules.

versions.notes: Concept archived from earlier Sprite/NOVA/NOMAD planning; no hardware completion claimed.

pieces.title: NOMAD — Electric Cargo Bike & Mobile Hub
pieces.summary: An electric cargo-bike concept serving as a portable edge-computing and field-work platform for exploration, power, sensors and local AI.
pieces.story: NOMAD was explored as a bike-based mobile hub for Project Sprite and S.A.G.E., alongside a portable/offline knowledge-node concept also called NOMAD. This entry tracks the bike-mounted physical direction without merging those ideas into a confirmed completed machine.
pieces.materials: Research candidates: cargo bicycle or e-cargo platform, weatherproof removable electronics enclosure, power management, mounting hardware, secured storage, field networking and sensors.
buildSteps: Clarify cycling, transport and field-work use cases
Choose an appropriate safe and legal bike platform
Test attachment, weight distribution and electrical safety
pieces.buildNotes: Concept only; bike specifications, ownership, power system and build status remain to be verified. Portable/offline node is a related but separate design direction.

versions.notes: Concept archived from earlier Sprite/NOVA/NOMAD planning; no hardware completion claimed.
